title: Course Page Template: User Guide
text:
Welcome to the SciLifeLab Training Template User Guide.
This guide explains how to customise the landing page and course pages without editing the template code.
By the end of this guide you will know how to:

Change the course title and subtitle
Configure the hero buttons
Add your organisation’s logo
Edit the course information cards
Configure course instances
Customise the course pages


0.0.1 Before you begin
This guide assumes that you have:

cloned the repository
installed the required software
can preview the template locally

Continue with Getting started to set up your local environment.

title: 2  Getting started
text:
3 The SciLifeLab Course Template
This repository publishes one website with two layers:
Examples:

title: 2  Getting started
text:
3.1 The Simple Model

main = landing page source
release-YYMM = one course instance
gh-pages = published output only

Use main when you want to change the landing page.
Use a release-YYMM branch when you want to change the actual course materials for one run.
Do not work directly on gh-pages unless you are recovering from a deployment problem.

title: 2  Getting started
text:
3.2 What Gets Deployed

Push to main

GitHub Actions renders the landing page.
The landing is published to the root of gh-pages.

Push to release-YYMM

GitHub Actions renders that course instance.
The instance is published to gh-pages/YYMM/.


The landing page does not auto-discover release branches. If you create a new instance branch, you must also update data/instances.yml on main if you want that instance to appear on the landing page.

title: 2  Getting started
text:
3.3 Which Files To Edit

3.3.1 Landing page on main
Edit these files for most landing-page changes:

index.qmd: top-level page shell
_sections/*.qmd: authored landing sections
styles.css: landing design and layout
data/instances.yml: current/previous instance links and visibility
data/ui.yml: landing UI labels

Dynamic partials are generated automatically:

_generated/hero-actions.qmd
_generated/instances-band.qmd

Do not edit _generated/* manually.


3.3.2 Course instance on release-YYMM
Edit the Quarto course files on that branch:

course .qmd pages
branch-local _quarto.yml
images and other branch-local course assets

title: 2  Getting started
text:
3.4 Common Workflows

3.4.1 1. Change the landing page

Work on main.
Edit the landing sections, styles, or landing data.
Run local checks:

python3 -m venv .venv
source .venv/bin/activate
python -m pip install --upgrade pip
python -m pip install -r requirements-dev.txt
python -m pytest -q
quarto render

Push main.
GitHub Actions publishes the updated landing root.



3.4.2 2. Create a new course instance

Create a new branch from release-0000.
Name it release-YYMM, for example release-2505.
Update the course content on that branch.
Push the branch.
GitHub Actions publishes that instance to gh-pages/YYMM/.
Update data/instances.yml on main so the landing page links to it.



3.4.3 3. Update an existing course instance

Checkout the relevant release-YYMM branch.
Edit the course materials.
Push the branch.
GitHub Actions republishes only that instance directory.



3.4.4 4. Change which instance is current on the landing page
Edit data/instances.yml on main.
Rules enforced by validation:

exactly one instance must have status: current
the current instance must have visible: true
relative instance URLs must match the slug

title: 2  Getting started
text:
3.5 How The Landing Is Built
The landing page is built in three layers:

Authored content

index.qmd
_sections/*.qmd

Data and generated fragments

data/instances.yml
data/ui.yml
scripts/generate_landing.py
_generated/*.qmd

Presentation

styles.css


Render flow:

quarto render starts
Quarto runs scripts/generate_landing.py as a pre-render step
the generator validates YAML data and writes _generated/*.qmd
index.qmd includes the authored sections
those sections include the generated fragments where needed
Quarto writes the final site to _site/

title: 2  Getting started
text:
3.6 GitHub Actions

.github/workflows/validate-landing.yml

runs on pull requests to main
runs tests, renders the landing, and checks that no raw YAML leaks into _site

.github/workflows/deploy-landing.yml

runs on push to main
publishes only landing-owned root files to gh-pages

.github/workflows/main.yml on release-* branches

runs on push to release branches
publishes only the matching instance directory to gh-pages

title: 2  Getting started
text:
3.7 Important Rules

gh-pages is machine-managed output
keep .nojekyll on gh-pages
never use a root-level deploy sync like rsync -a --delete _site/ gh-pages/
keep raw YAML out of published output
update data/instances.yml on main when instance visibility changes

title: 3  Landing page
section: 3.1 Hero: Change the course title and subtitle
text:
3.1 Hero: Change the course title and subtitle
The hero is the large banner at the top of the landing page. It is the first thing visitors see when they open your course website and contains the course title, subtitle, logos, and ‘current course instance’ and ‘registration’ action buttons.

3.1.1 Change the course title

In the main branch, open the _sections folder and then the file hero.qmd.
Locate the following lines:

:::{.hero__title}
Course title
:::

Replace Course title with the title of your course.



3.1.2 Change the course subtitle

In the main branch, open the _sections folder and then the file hero.qmd.
Locate the following lines:

:::{.hero__subtitle}
Course subtitle
:::

Replace Course subtitle with a one-line description of your course.







Tip



Keep the subtitle to one sentence and start with an action verb such as Learn, Understand, Explore, Build, or Apply.
For example:

Learn how to apply open science practices throughout the research lifecycle.




 Quick reference 
 Change course title and subtitle

Replace the text between :::{.hero__title} and :::.

title: 3  Landing page
section: 3.2 Hero: Add or remove a logo
text:
3.2 Hero: Add or remove a logo
The logos displayed in the hero banner represent the organisations associated with your course. You can add additional logos, remove existing ones, or replace them with your own.

3.2.1 Add a logo

Save your logo as a PNG or SVG file.







Tip



If possible, use a white version of your logo so that it contrasts well with the dark background of the hero banner.



In the main branch, open the img folder, then the logos folder.
Copy your logo file into the folder.

VS Code: Drag and drop the file into the folder.
GitHub Desktop: Click Add file, then Upload files.

In the main branch, open the _sections folder and then the file hero.qmd.
Locate the following block:

<div class="hero__brand-item">
  <img src="img/logos/SciLifeLab_Logotype_NEG.png"
       alt="SciLifeLab"
       class="hero__partner-logo">
</div>

Copy the entire block and paste it directly below the existing one.
Replace only the src and alt values with those for your own logo.

For example:
<div class="hero__brand-item">
  <img src="img/logos/your-logo-file.png"
       alt="Your organisation"
       class="hero__partner-logo">
</div>


3.2.2 Remove a logo

In the main branch, open the _sections folder and then the file hero.qmd.
Locate the logo block you want to remove.

For example:
<div class="hero__brand-item">
  <img src="img/logos/SciLifeLab_Logotype_NEG.png"
       alt="SciLifeLab"
       class="hero__partner-logo">
</div>

Delete the entire <div class="hero__brand-item">...</div> block.
OPTIONAL: If you no longer need the logo image, you can also delete it from the img/logos folder.


VS Code: Right-click the file and select Delete.
GitHub Desktop: Open the repository, locate the file, click the three dots (⋮), and choose Delete file.


 Quick reference 
 Add or remove a logo

Delete an unused logo file (optional)

Delete the logo image if it is no longer needed.

title: 3  Landing page
section: 3.3 Hero: Configure the current course instance and registration action buttons
text:
3.3 Hero: Configure the current course instance and registration action buttons
The hero can display two action buttons:

Take me to the current course instance links visitors to the current published course instance.
Register now links visitors to the course registration page.

You can change these buttons’ links and text, or hide them when they are not needed.

3.3.1 Add a link to the current course instance button

In the main branch, open the data folder and then the file instances.yml.
Locate the course instance with:

status: current

Update slug, label, instance_url, and sort_key to match the current course instance. The values of slug and instance_url must match!

For example:
instances:
  - slug: "0000"
    label: "May 2026"
    status: current
    visible: true
    show_in_hero: true
    instance_url: "./0000/"
    registration_url: "https://example.org/registration"
    sort_key: 200000
For a course instance taught in May 2026, this could become:
instances:
  - slug: "2605"
    label: "May 2026"
    status: current
    visible: true
    show_in_hero: true
    instance_url: "./2605/"
    registration_url: "https://example.org/registration"
    sort_key: 202605






Tip



In this template, each course instance is generated from a repository branch and is named using the year and month in which the instance is taught.
For example, a course taught in May 2026 uses 2605. Its relative course instance URL is therefore ./2605/.




3.3.2 Add a link to the registration button
If registration for your training is open, you can display the Register now button and link it directly to your registration page.

In the main branch, open the data folder and then the file instances.yml.
Locate the course instance with:

status: current

Find registration_url:

registration_url: "https://example.org/registration"

Replace the example URL with the URL of your course registration page.

For example:
registration_url: "https://your-registration-page.example"


3.3.3 Hide the current course instance button
If you don’t have a current course instance (e.g. if the course is self-paced or dormant), you can hide the current course instance button.

In data/instances.yml, locate the current course instance and change:

show_in_hero: true
to:
show_in_hero: false
The current course instance can remain in instances.yml; it will simply no longer be displayed as a button in the hero.


3.3.4 Hide the registration button
If the registration for your training is closed, or if the training doesn’t require registration, you can hide the registration button.

In data/instances.yml, change:

registration_url: "https://example.org/registration"
to:
registration_url: ""
An empty registration_url tells the template not to display the registration button.


3.3.5 Change action button text
You can also change the text displayed inside either action button without changing where the button links.

In the main branch, open the data folder and then the file ui.yml.
Locate:

hero_view_current_label: Take me to the current course instance
hero_registration_open_label: Register now

Replace the text after the colon with the text you want to display.

For example:
hero_view_current_label: View the latest course
hero_registration_open_label: Register for the course
Do not change the names hero_view_current_label or hero_registration_open_label. Only change the text after the colon.

Quick reference

title: 3  Landing page
text:
3.4 Course information cards: edit text
The information cards below the hero banner provide key information about your course, including the course content, learning outcomes, topics covered, keywords, course founders, and contributors. Each card can be edited independently.

3.4.1 Change the course content card

In the main branch, open the _sections folder and then the file top-cards.qmd.
Find the Course content card.
Under:

:::{.card-copy}
Description of the content of the course

Lorem ipsum dolor sit amet, consectetur adipiscing elit...
replace the example text with a description of your course.






Tip



Keep the course description concise and focus on what the course covers. Around 10 sentences is usually enough.




3.4.2 Change the learning outcomes card

In the main branch, open the _sections folder and then the file top-cards.qmd.
Find the Learning outcomes card.
Under:

:::{.card-copy}
1. Learning outcome 1
2. Learning outcome 2
3. Learning outcome 3
replace the example learning outcomes with the learning outcomes for your course.






Tip



Learning outcomes should describe what participants will be able to do after completing the course.
For guidance on writing learning outcomes, see the SciLifeLab Training Hub resource on writing learning outcomes.




3.4.3 Change the keywords card

In the main branch, open the _sections folder and then the file top-cards.qmd.
Find the Keywords card.
Under:

:::{.card-copy}
- Keyword 1
- Keyword 2
replace the example keywords with keywords that describe your course.






Tip



Around four or five keywords is usually enough. Choose short terms that describe the main subject areas of the course.




3.4.4 Change the topics covered cards

In the main branch, open the _sections folder and then the file top-cards.qmd.
Find the Topics covered card.
Under:

:::{.card-copy}
- Topic 1
- Topic 2
replace the example topics with the main topics covered by your course.






Tip



Use short phrases rather than complete sentences. Aim to give visitors a quick overview of the main subjects covered by the course.




3.4.5 Change the course founders card
The Course founders card can be used to acknowledge the people who originally developed or established the course.

In the main branch, open the _sections folder and then the file bottom-cards.qmd.
Find the Course founders card.
Under:

:::{.card-copy}
- Course founder 1
- Course founder 2
replace the example names with the names of the course founders.


3.4.6 Change the course contributors
The Contributors card can be used to acknowledge people who have contributed to the development or maintenance of the course.

In the main branch, open the _sections folder and then the file bottom-cards.qmd.
Find the Contributors card.
Under:

:::{.card-copy}
- Contributor 1
- Contributor 2
replace the example names with the names of the course contributors.

title: 3  Landing page
text:
3.5 Manage course instances
The All course instances banner provides links to the different published instances of your course. This allows visitors to access the current course instance, as well as previous course instances that you choose to make available.
Course instances are managed in data/instances.yml. The instance marked as current is also used for the Take me to the current course instance action button in the hero. Some of the settings described in this section therefore overlap with the instructions for configuring the hero buttons.






Important




Each course instance must have a unique slug. Do not use the same slug for more than one instance!
Only one course instance should be marked as:

status: current

The instance marked as current determines which course instance is treated as the current course throughout the landing page, including the link used by the hero action button. See Mark a course instance as current for instructions.




3.5.1 Add a new course instance

In the main branch, open the data folder and then the file instances.yml.
Copy a full existing course instance entry.
Paste the copied entry under instances:.
Update the slug, label, instance_url and sort key values to describe the new course instance.

For example, for a new course instance taught in November 2026:
- slug: "2611"
  label: "November 2026"
  status: current
  visible: true
  show_in_hero: true
  instance_url: "./2611/"
  registration_url: "https://example.org/registration"
  sort_key: 202611


3.5.2 Mark a course instance as current

In the main branch, open the data folder and then the file instances.yml.
Find the previous current instance.
Change:

status: current
to:
status: previous

Set the new current instance to:

status: current
For example:
instances:
  - slug: "2611"
    label: "November 2026"
    status: current
    visible: true
    show_in_hero: true
    instance_url: "./2611/"
    registration_url: "https://example.org/registration"
    sort_key: 202611

  - slug: "2605"
    label: "May 2026"
    status: previous
    visible: true
    show_in_hero: false
    instance_url: "./2605/"
    registration_url: ""
    sort_key: 202605


3.5.3 Show or hide a previous instance in the All course instances banner

In the main branch, open the data folder and then the file instances.yml.
To display an instance in the banner:

visible: true

To hide an instance in the banner:

visible: false
Hiding an instance does not delete it from instances.yml. It simply prevents it from being displayed in the banner.






Important



The instance marked as:
status: current
must always remain:
visible: true
Do not hide the current course instance by setting visible: false. If you do not want the current instance to appear as a button in the hero, use:
show_in_hero: false
instead.




3.5.4 Change the course instance name displayed in the banner

In the main branch, open the data folder and then the file instances.yml.
Change the value for label For example:

label: "May 2026"
can be changed to:
label: "November 2026"
Changing the label only changes the text visitors see. It does not change the course instance URL.


3.5.5 Change the order of course instances
The sort_key determines the chronological order of the course instances.

In the main branch, open the data folder and then the file instances.yml.
Change the value for sort_key. Use the format

YYYYMM
For example:
sort_key: 202605
represents May 2026.

title: 3  Landing page
text:
3.6 Edit the footer
The footer at the bottom of the landing page contains information about the course page development, its licence, and a link to the course repository on GitHub.

3.6.1 Change the footer text

In the main branch, open the _sections folder and then the file footer.qmd.
Locate:

By SciLifeLab Training Hub. Licensed under [CC BY 4.0](https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/).

Built with Quarto and hosted on GitHub Pages.

Replace the text with the information you want to display in the footer.







Tip



If you use a licence other than CC BY 4.0, update both the licence name and its link.
In [CC BY 4.0](https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/):

replace the text between [ ] with the name of the licence;
replace the URL between ( ) with the corresponding licence URL.





3.6.2 Change the GitHub repository link
The GitHub logo in the footer links visitors to the course repository.

In the main branch, open the _sections folder and then the file footer.qmd.
Locate:

<a href="https://github.com/SciLifeLab-Training/scilifelab-training-template-staging/tree/main" class="landing-footer__image-link">

Replace only the URL inside href="..." with the URL of your course repository.

For example:
<a href="https://github.com/your-organisation/your-course/tree/main" class="landing-footer__image-link">

Quick reference

title: 4  FAIRification and publishing your course
section: 4.2 Make your materials easy to cite
text:
4.2 Make your materials easy to cite
To make your training easier to cite, you can provide citation information in a CITATION.cff file. This file contains structured information about how your training materials should be cited, including the course title, authors, ORCID identifiers, licence, and links to the course repository and website.

4.2.1 Create the citation file for your course
The SciLifeLab Course Page Template already contains a CITATION.cff file in the root of the repository on the main branch. This file describes the template itself. When you use the template for your own course, replace the contents of CITATION.cff with citation information for your own training materials.

In the main branch, open CITATION.cff.
Delete the existing contents of the file.
Copy and paste the following starter text:

cff-version: 1.2.0
message: "If you use these training materials, please cite them as below."

title: "COURSE TITLE"

authors:
  - family-names: "SURNAME"
    given-names: "GIVEN NAME"
    orcid: "https://orcid.org/0000-0000-0000-0000"

license: CC-BY-4.0

repository-code: "https://github.com/ORGANISATION/REPOSITORY"
url: "https://ORGANISATION.github.io/REPOSITORY/"

references:
  - type: software
    title: "SciLifeLab Course Page Template"
    repository-code: "PERMANENT TEMPLATE REPOSITORY URL"

Replace the placeholder values with information about your course.








Field
What to enter




title
The title of your course or training materials.


family-names
The author’s family name or surname.


given-names
The author’s given name(s).


orcid
The author’s ORCID identifier, if they have one.


license
The licence under which the training materials are made available.


repository-code
The URL of the GitHub repository containing your course materials.


url
The URL of the published course website.









Important



Keep:
cff-version: 1.2.0
unchanged. This is the version of the Citation File Format specification, not the version of your course.




4.2.2 Add multiple authors
Add a separate entry under authors for each person who should be credited as an author of the training materials.
For example:
authors:
  - family-names: "Smith"
    given-names: "Anna"
    orcid: "https://orcid.org/0000-0000-0000-0000"

  - family-names: "Jones"
    given-names: "David"
    orcid: "https://orcid.org/0000-0000-0000-0000"
If an author does not have an ORCID, simply omit the orcid line:
authors:
  - family-names: "Jones"
    given-names: "David"






Tip



ORCID provides researchers with a persistent identifier that distinguishes them from other researchers. If your contributors have ORCID identifiers, include them in CITATION.cff.




4.2.3 Acknowledge this template in your course
The starter file contains the following entry:
references:
  - type: software
    title: "SciLifeLab Course Page Template"
    repository-code: "PERMANENT TEMPLATE REPOSITORY URL"
Keep this entry when adapting CITATION.cff for your course. It acknowledges the SciLifeLab Course Page Template as the resource used to create your course website.


4.2.4 Citation files for individual course instances
How you manage CITATION.cff depends on how you publish your course materials.
If your course is maintained as one continuously updated resource, you can maintain the citation information in the main branch.
If individual course instances are released separately (in this template by adding and publishing branches), their citation information may also differ. For example, different instances may have different contributors.
In this case, update CITATION.cff in the specific course-instance branch before creating the release. This allows the citation metadata for that release to reflect the people and materials associated with that particular course instance.






Tip



Before publishing a course instance, check that CITATION.cff contains the correct title, authors, ORCIDs, licence, repository URL, and course website URL for the materials you are releasing.



Quick reference
 Make your course citable 








To…
File
Edit




Add citation information for your course
CITATION.cff
Replace the template citation metadata with the starter CFF and enter your course information.


Add an author
CITATION.cff
Add another entry under authors.


Add an ORCID
CITATION.cff
Add the author’s ORCID using the orcid field.


Credit an author without an ORCID
CITATION.cff
Include their name and omit the orcid field.


Cite a particular course instance

Update the citation metadata before creating the release.
